o1.biggest_strength: Targets the Essentials 8+ churn pocket with a flat Agency plan and a clean two-arm test, and the customer email is in real Buffer voice.
o1.biggest_mistake: Its math mixes per-customer revenue with per-1,000-customer projections in a way that is hard to reconcile, and the '$23,900 lost each month' figure is squishy (9.6% x $257k is closer to $24.7k).
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Show the revenue math on a single, consistent base so the owner can trace the first two-quarters gain straight to the churn-reduction number.

o2.biggest_strength: Clear base and downside cases, an explicit '1 in 3 Team downgrades kills it' threshold, and a test that also measures Team downgrade risk instead of hiding it.
o2.biggest_mistake: The $79 vs $66 yearly pricing is internally inconsistent with 'two months free' and its own Agency revenue assumption ($76.53), so the headline price and the math don't line up.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the yearly price and the blended Agency revenue assumption agree, and trim one risk section so the core decision reads in one pass.

reason: Both land the right call, but Output 2 shows the downside case and the Team-downgrade break-even in one place, which is what I'd want before signing off, even though its yearly price needs fixing.
